icon-button.name: Icon Button
icon-button.purpose: Use Icon Button for compact icon-only topbar utilities such as language, grid, and contrast. The component owns circular hit area, accessible name, optional selected/toggle state, focus, disabled, and press feedback.
icon-button.referenceRationale: The ZIP reference gives the visual benchmark: circular icon-only control, 36/44/52px density scale, selected glyph fill, tonal surface, badge dot, hover/press scale, and spring motion. Design System keeps ownership of tokens, foundations, state precedence, accessibility, and documentation rules.

anatomy.rule: Provides the action name because the visible UI is icon-only.
Owns fixed square hit area, circle radius, background, border, focus, and density.
Uses one Design System icon and inherits currentColor from the button state.
Shows a pressed/toggle state through aria-pressed, accent color, and filled glyph.
Adds a small live indicator without replacing the accessible name.

variants.description: Transparent surface for low-emphasis toolbar actions.
Subtle surface and border for persistent utilities or selected state.
High-emphasis icon action with primary surface.
Expressive action where accent color is product-approved.

intents.description: Destructive icon action that still needs accessible confirmation.
Risky icon action that needs review or caution context.

icon-button.statePrecedence: disabled > focus > pressed > selected > hover > badged > default

Energy.decision: Use Energy for surface, icon color, selected accent, badge, and disabled state.
Energy.behavior: Energy keeps compact actions visible without labels.
Energy.example: Grid and contrast controls show selected state in the topbar.
Energy.test: Verify icon, surface, badge, selected, and disabled contrast.
Energy.rejectIf: Raw color or color-only state replaces tokens.

Voice.decision: Use Voice indirectly through accessible name and tooltip text.
Voice.test: Verify every icon button has a clear accessible name.
Voice.rejectIf: The icon is the only name.

Frame.decision: Use Frame for circular size, hit area, border, radius, badge position, and density.
Frame.behavior: Frame prevents compact toolbars from shrinking below touch targets.
Frame.example: Topbar utilities keep a fixed circular control.
Frame.test: Verify 3 density contexts without layout shift.
Frame.rejectIf: Icon size or badge changes the hit area.

Depth.decision: Use Depth only for tonal/raised context when the variant requires a surface.
Depth.behavior: Depth separates utility action from page background without inventing state.
Depth.example: Tonal icon button sits on documentation chrome.
Depth.test: Verify shadow never replaces selected or focus.
Depth.rejectIf: Depth is used as the only interaction state.

Momentum.decision: Use Momentum for hover scale, press scale, selected glyph fill, and badge pulse.
Momentum.behavior: Motion confirms the tap quickly without delaying action.
Momentum.example: Pressed state scales down and selected state fills the glyph.
Momentum.rejectIf: Motion hides state or uses raw curves.

State.decision: Use State for disabled, focus, pressed, selected, hover, badged, and default precedence.
State.behavior: State makes toggle buttons machine-readable through aria-pressed.
State.test: Verify aria-pressed, focus, disabled, and click behavior.

Tone.decision: Use Tone for concise accessible labels and tooltip language.
Tone.behavior: Tone clarifies the action behind the symbol.
Tone.example: Use 'Switch language' for the language button.
Tone.test: Verify labels say the action, not the icon name.
Tone.rejectIf: Copy is ambiguous or icon jargon.

Growth.decision: Use Growth for reusable toolbar utilities across docs, prototypes, and product shells.
Growth.behavior: Growth keeps compact controls portable as toolbars multiply.
Growth.example: Language, grid, and contrast controls share one contract while search remains an input.
Growth.test: Verify the same API works across products.
Growth.rejectIf: Each toolbar forks a one-off utility control.

Symbol.decision: Use Symbol for the glyph contract and filled selected mode.
Symbol.behavior: Symbol keeps icon choice and fill state systematic.
Symbol.test: Verify icon names map to approved symbols.
Symbol.rejectIf: Custom glyphs bypass the icon system.

Iconography.decision: Use Iconography for size, optical alignment, and currentColor inheritance.
Iconography.behavior: Iconography keeps the symbol readable in mobile topbars.
Iconography.example: Mobile tab icons use the same minimum symbol scale.
Iconography.test: Verify icon legibility at sm, md, and lg.
Iconography.rejectIf: Icons are too small to read or use negative spacing.

Accessibility.decision: Use Accessibility for aria-label, aria-pressed, focus, disabled, badge announcement, and touch target.
Accessibility.behavior: Accessibility makes icon-only UI understandable for humans and agents.
Accessibility.example: A selected contrast button announces pressed state.
Accessibility.test: Verify name, role, pressed state, focus, disabled, and target size.
Accessibility.rejectIf: The control has no accessible name or hidden state.

props.name: icon
props.notes: Approved Design System/Material Symbols glyph name.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.notes: Accessible action name because there is no visible text.

props.name: density
props.notes: Design System Density context for the fixed circular hit area.

productExamples.example: Grid and contrast expose selected state when active.
Language remains a compact action while search stays an input.

do: Use for one compact icon-only action.
Use selected only when the button behaves like a toggle.
dont: Do not use for text actions.
Do not hide destructive meaning behind an unlabeled icon.
Do not use selected for momentary actions.
info: Switch remains the component for persistent on/off settings. SegmentedControl belongs later as a compound navigation/control pattern.

contextDensityStrategy.layout: minimum visible utilities with touch-size circular controls
toolbar clusters with selected state and badge support
remote-focus or pointer utility bars with large hit areas

agentInstructions: Use Icon Button for compact icon-only utilities with an accessible name.
Use selected only when the utility is a toggle button with aria-pressed.
Do not treat search input, menu navigation, or multi-option controls as Icon Button examples.
rejectIf: Selected state is not exposed as aria-pressed.
A Switch setting is implemented as Icon Button.
A multi-option SegmentedControl is treated as one Icon Button.
Icon, badge, or state changes resize the hit area.
